title: Isandro and the Atlas
premise: In 1847, apprentice mapmaker Quentin Kavanagh completes the atlas his master died protecting, only to discover a sealed letter hidden in its binding that names the Kavanagh family as targets of a political purge. As soldiers close in on the river town, Quentin must use the atlas's secret routes to smuggle his family toward the last ferry berth before the ice breaks. In the end, he gives the berth to his younger sister and stays behind, choosing exile over belonging — but the atlas he carries becomes proof that identity survives even when home does not.
about_author: Mara Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing nineteenth-century cartographic collections before turning to fiction. She writes historical novels about the quiet people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Weight of Blank Paper
chapters.summary: Quentin finishes the final plate of his dead master's atlas, hiding his grief in precise linework. When he finds the sealed letter stitched into the binding, its accusations against the Kavanagh family shatter his sense of safety. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: dread disguised as diligence — the moment a life's work becomes evidence against him.

chapters.title: Which Silences Keep People Safe
chapters.summary: Quentin confronts his uncle, who admits the family's old allegiances but begs him to burn the letter. Soldiers arrive asking questions about the master's death, and Quentin realizes the atlas itself is what they want. He begins memorizing secret routes. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: fractured trust; loyalty and fear pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Ice Begins to Break
chapters.summary: With the river thawing and one berth left on the last ferry, Quentin leads his family through back channels marked only in the atlas. A betrayal by a neighbor forces them into the open, and soldiers corner them at the dock. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: rising panic and resolve — every choice now costs someone everything.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: At the dock, Quentin puts his sister aboard and stays behind to draw the soldiers away, surrendering the atlas's routes from memory under interrogation. Exiled but unbroken, he walks north with blank paper and begins mapping a new country for himself. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into identity — belonging carried within, not granted by place.
